newsitem.title: USA: AT&T drops on earnings warning, downgrades.
newsitem.headline: AT&T drops on earnings warning, downgrades.

text.p: AT&T Corp shares continued thier steep decline in midday trading after the company issued a warning about earnings for the third and fourth quarters, prompting several Wall Street analysts to slash their ratings on the stock.
The stock fell 5-1/4 to 52 on volume of 8.6 million shares, making it the most actively traded issue on the New York Stock Exchange.
AT&T Corp said in a statement on Tuesday that third quarter share earnings may fall 10 percent below analysts' estimates, and fourth quarter results could also fall short by a comparable amount.
AT&T cited stiff competition in its key long-distance telephone business, as well as pressure on revenues and higher marketing costs.
PaineWebber and Prudential reduced their ratings on the stock. Prudential analyst Michael Elling said he cut the stock to hold from buy.
"Management has been given every opportunity to perform, and has not performed," Elling said. "I would be looking for management changes....sooner rather than later."
Elling added that ATT "has a lot of strengths."

"I still like the company long term," he said. "It has a lot going for it. To draw on a football analogy, it's third down and long. I never expected them to get the first down, but I did expect an effort, and not fumble the ball."

Elling said he slashed the rating to hold from buy, and reduced his earnings estimates to $3.51 per share from $3.75 for 1996, and to $3.60 from $4.25 for 1997. AT&T had net income per share of $0.09 in 1995.
PaineWebber cut the rating to neutral from attractive, according to a PaineWebber source.
